title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: OpenScholar's iterative self-feedback retrieval-augmented inference pipeline generates outputs with inline citations linked to specific passages from scientific literature, enabling researchers to trace output back to original literature and ensuring transparency and verifiability.
evidence_quote: These citations allow researchers to trace the output back to the original literature, ensuring transparency and verifiability.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: OpenScholar includes a citation verification step where the generator LM ensures all citation-worthy statements are supported by references from retrieved passages, performing post hoc insertion for unsupported claims.
evidence_quote: the generator ensures that all citation-worthy statements—scientific claims requiring justification—are adequately supported by references from the retrieved passages. If any claims lack proper citations, the LM performs a post hoc insertion to ensure that citation-worthy statements are supported by passages.
section: Section 2.2 (Inference: Iterative Generation with Retrieval-Augmented Self-Feedback)

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: The OpenScholar-Datastore (OSDS) is built from 45 million papers using peS2o v3, producing 234 million passages — described as the largest open-sourced datastore for scientific literature.
evidence_quote: we use peS2o v3, which includes 45 million papers up until October 2024. ... Our datastore consists of 234 million passages. To our knowledge, this is the largest open-sourced datastore for scientific literature.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: The authors open-source all components — code, data, model checkpoints, datastores, and the SCHOLARQABENCH benchmark — to support reproducibility and accelerate future research.
evidence_quote: We open-source the OPENSCHOLAR code, data, model checkpoints, datastores, and SCHOLARQABENCH, along with a public demo, to support and accelerate future research efforts.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: High-quality training data is generated synthetically using the inference-time pipeline, with a two-step data filtering process (pairwise-filtering and rubric-filtering) to remove hallucinations and repetitive writing.
evidence_quote: Despite its effectiveness and scalability, synthetic data may also contain issues such as hallucinations, repetitive writing, or limited instruction-following ... we introduce a two-step data filtering process: pairwise-filtering and rubric-filtering

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: Non-retrieval augmented LLMs fabricate 78–98% of cited papers, with the problem exacerbated in biomedical domains; even when citations refer to real papers, the majority are not substantiated by corresponding abstracts, resulting in near-zero citation accuracy.
evidence_quote: the proportion of cited papers that actually exist is strikingly low. In particular, while models such as GPT4o and Llama can generate plausible reference lists, we find that 78-98% of the cited papers are fabricated, and the issue is exacerbated in biomedical domains.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: OpenScholar-8B achieves zero hallucinated papers in both computer science and biomedicine, in stark contrast to baseline LLMs (Llama 3.1 8B: 92.1% CS, 97.6% Bio hallucination ratios).

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: The self-feedback mechanism iteratively refines outputs: the LM generates an initial response, self-feedback, and incorporates feedback to produce an updated response, addressing unsupported claims and incomplete outputs.
evidence_quote: this one-step generation can lead to unsupported claims (Liu et al., 2023) or incomplete output due to missing information (Asai et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2023). To address these challenges, in OPENSCHOLAR, we introduce an iterative generation approach with self-feedback
section: Section 2.2 (Inference: Iterative Generation with Retrieval-Augmented Self-Feedback)

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: SCHOLARQABENCH introduces a multifaceted automatic evaluation pipeline measuring Correctness, Citation accuracy (precision/recall/F1), and content quality (Relevance, Coverage, Organization) across 2,967 queries in 4 scientific disciplines.
evidence_quote: We developed a multifaceted automatic evaluation pipeline to facilitate reproducible and efficient evaluations, complementing expert assessments.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: Human evaluation involved 16 Ph.D.-level expert annotators across three scientific disciplines, producing over 400 fine-grained evaluations; OS-GPT4o was rated Useful in 80% of queries and preferred over human answers in 70% of cases.
evidence_quote: A total of 16 expert annotators from the three fields contributed to our evaluations ... OPENSCHOLAR-GPT4o and OPENSCHOLAR-8B are rated as Useful in 80% and 72% of the queries, respectively.

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: Limitation: OpenScholar does not consistently retrieve the most representative or relevant papers for certain queries; expert annotators noted citations were occasionally outdated or less relevant.
evidence_quote: OPENSCHOLAR does not consistently retrieve the most representative or relevant papers for certain queries. ... annotators also noted that the citations provided by models could be improved, pointing out that the suggested papers were occasionally outdated or less relevant

title: OpenScholar: Synthesizing Scientific Literature with Retrieval-Augmented LMs
claim_text: Limitation: The evaluation dataset with human-written answers is relatively small (110 for CS-LFQA, 108 for expert-written answers), potentially introducing statistical variance; SCHOLARQABENCH focuses only on CS, biomedicine, and physics.
evidence_quote: the evaluation dataset with human-written answers is relatively small (e.g., 110 for CS-LFQA and 108 for expert-written answers). This limited dataset may introduce statistical variance ... SCHOLARQABENCH primarily focuses on computer science, biomedicine, and physics, with no instances from social sciences

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: LatteReview's ReviewWorkflow class orchestrates multi-stage review processes with sequential rounds, parallel reviews, conditional filtering, and output aggregation — providing structured provenance for each decision.
evidence_quote: The ReviewWorkflow class allows users to define multi-stage review processes with: Sequential Rounds: Execute reviews in predefined stages, where the output of one stage can feed into the next. Parallel Reviews: Assign multiple reviewers to independently assess the same inputs.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: Reasoning transparency is built into the TitleAbstractReviewer agent, which provides either brief or chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning for its inclusion/exclusion decisions — reasoning cannot be None.
evidence_quote: the agent provides reasoning for its decisions, which could be 'brief' or 'cot', where the former means the agent should return a brief reasoning in 1-2 sentences, and the latter means a more detailed step-by-step reasoning is expected in the Chain-of-thought format. ... the reasoning cannot be None for the TitleAbstractReviewer.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: LatteReview integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflows, allowing reviewers to dynamically fetch relevant information and incorporate retrieved data into the review process for grounding.
evidence_quote: LatteReview integrates seamlessly with retrieval-augmented generation workflows, enabling reviewers to: Leverage External Knowledge: Fetch relevant information dynamically to enhance review accuracy. Dynamic Context Addition: Automatically incorporate retrieved data for each input item into the review process.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: The framework is open-source and available on GitHub and PyPI, enabling reproducible installations and community contributions.
evidence_quote: LatteReview is designed to be straightforward to install ... The package is available on PyPI and can be installed using the following command: pip install lattereview ... For users requiring additional functionalities, LatteReview provides optional extras

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: The TitleAbstractReviewer uses a 5-point Likert scale for article assessment (1 = absolutely exclude, 5 = absolutely include), with hierarchical decision-making: when junior reviewers disagree, a senior reviewer's assessment becomes definitive.
evidence_quote: The TitleAbstractReviewer agents in our workflow employ a 5-point Likert scale for article assessment ... when the junior reviewers' scores differ or both assign a score of 3, the senior reviewer's assessment is sought and becomes definitive.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: The framework encourages human oversight, recommending researchers break reviews into stages with manual review checkpoints rather than pursuing fully automated end-to-end processes.
evidence_quote: it's crucial to design your LatteReview workflows with human oversight in mind. Rather than aiming for a fully automated end-to-end process, consider breaking your review into stages punctuated by manual review.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: Evaluation on six SYNERGY datasets showed AUC values ranging from 0.77 to 0.95, with performance varying significantly across datasets due to task heterogeneity, dataset characteristics, and threshold sensitivity.
evidence_quote: The review workflow demonstrated substantial discriminative capability, achieving Area Under the Curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.77 to 0.95 across the six different article collections ... we observed significant variation in performance across datasets.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: A review workflow of two junior reviewers (Gemini-1.5-flash and GPT-4O-mini) reviewing 1,000 title/abstract pairs took approximately one minute at a cost of $1.20.
evidence_quote: a review workflow consisting of two junior reviewers using Gemini 1.5 Flash and OpenAI GPT-4O-mini ... took, on average, about one minute to review 1,000 pairs of titles and abstracts, at a cost of $1.20.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: Limitation: Performance variability across datasets is attributed to task heterogeneity, dataset size differences, varying inclusion rates (from <1% to 12.36%), and threshold sensitivity — the choice of decision threshold significantly impacts performance.
evidence_quote: This variability can be attributed to several key factors: Task Heterogeneity ... Dataset Characteristics: The datasets exhibit substantial heterogeneity in both size and inclusion rates ... Threshold Sensitivity: ... the choice of decision threshold significantly impacts the review workflow's performance.

title: LatteReview: A Multi-Agent Framework for Systematic Reviews
claim_text: Future development priorities include supporting a broader range of language models, enhancing memory and context management, creating a no-code interface, and providing more advanced validation tools.
evidence_quote: Future development will focus on expanding LatteReview's capabilities and accessibility. Priorities include supporting a broader range of language models, facilitating improved collaboration between agents and users, and enhancing memory and context management to refine decision-making processes.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: The pipeline is fully local and zero-shot, running on consumer-grade hardware (Apple M1 Max) with the gpt-oss-20b model via Ollama, requiring no cloud APIs or proprietary models — enabling full reproducibility.
evidence_quote: This study benchmarked a fully local, zero-shot, schema-constrained LLM pipeline for title/abstract screening and abstract-based extraction and synthesis under reproducibility and privacy constraints on consumer-grade hardware.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: Schema-constrained extraction uses fixed prompts and structured enumerations rather than free generation, with conservative missingness handling (returning 'NR') to minimize fabrication and ensure deterministic outputs.
evidence_quote: schema enforcement (constrained enumerations rather than free generation) and conservative missingness handling (returning 'NR') were designed to minimize fabrication and performed well in audited fields.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: The pipeline couples screening with structured abstract-level extraction and high-level synthesis using fixed prompts and schemas, operationalizing a local-first workflow that does not depend on proprietary cloud models.
evidence_quote: the present work operationalizes a local-first workflow that couples screening with structured abstract-level extraction and high-level synthesis using fixed prompts and schemas.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: On the ketamine/neuroimaging benchmark, the pipeline achieved 100% recall, 97.9% precision, 99.4% accuracy, and 98.9% F1 — the best performance across all three benchmarks.
evidence_quote: Recall/Precision/Accuracy/F1 (%) 100.0/97.9/99.4/98.9

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: Performance tracked the density and explicitness of source text: when constructs were explicitly encoded in abstracts, maximal sensitivity was achieved; when outcomes were inconsistently reported, screening was rate-limited by missing or underspecified inputs.
evidence_quote: performance tracked the density and explicitness of the source text: when the construct of interest was explicitly encoded in abstracts (ketamine-neuroimaging), the pipeline achieved maximal sensitivity with high precision ... when outcomes were inconsistently reported at abstract level (clozapine-suicidality; clozapine experiences), screening and synthesis were predictably rate-limited by missing or underspecified inputs.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: Schema enforcement and conservative missingness handling were specifically designed to minimize hallucination risk, and performed well in audited fields — residual hallucination risk remains but is addressed through structural constraints.
evidence_quote: Residual hallucination risk also remains [25,26], although schema enforcement (constrained enumerations rather than free generation) and conservative missingness handling (returning 'NR') were designed to minimize fabrication and performed well in audited fields.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: Limitation: The evaluation was proof-of-concept benchmarking against three published systematic reviews rather than fully independent external validation against a prospective gold standard; single-author adjudication was used without blinded dual review.
evidence_quote: The present evaluation should be understood as proof-of-concept workflow benchmarking against three published systematic reviews, rather than as fully independent external validation against a prospective gold standard. The three benchmarks were not a random sample of psychiatry domains, single-author adjudication was used without blinded dual review

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: The central trade-off is reduced mechanistic resolution relative to full-text synthesis; abstract-only processing entails partial information loss but yields major gains in feasibility, governance, and scalability beyond human limits.
evidence_quote: A consistent methodological trade-off emerged across the three targets: abstract-only processing entails partial information loss relative to full text [20-22], but yields major gains in the feasibility of retrieval, governance, and scalability well beyond human limits.

title: Benchmarking a Local Schema-Constrained Large Language Model Pipeline for Systematic Scoping Reviews
claim_text: A pragmatic deployment model is recommended: high-throughput abstract-level mapping for coverage, paired with periodic human audits and targeted full-text deep dives where abstract informativeness is low or clinical stakes are high.
evidence_quote: A pragmatic deployment model is therefore hybrid: high-throughput abstract-level mapping for coverage, paired with periodic human audits and targeted full-text deep dives where abstract informativeness is low or clinical stakes are high

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: The multi-agent system operates through four sequential agents: (1) search string generation agent, (2) paper selection agent, (3) data extraction agent, and (4) data compilation agent — each with a defined role and handoff.
evidence_quote: The process begins with the input of a research topic ... the system systematically generates a pertinent set of research questions ... the system proceeds to generate a search string ... the subsequent phase involves retrieving papers ... the system extracts data based on the formulated RQs.

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: The paper selection agent applies inclusive and exclusive filtering criteria based on titles to refine search results, ensuring only the most pertinent literature is considered.
evidence_quote: the system is equipped with the capability to apply inclusive and exclusive criteria based on titles, which further refines the search results to ensure only the most pertinent literature is considered for review.

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: The system's standardization of the SLR process can potentially lead to more consistent and replicable research outcomes, though it requires human oversight in guiding and interpreting results.
evidence_quote: the system's standardization of the SLR process can potentially lead to more consistent and replicable research outcomes, a cornerstone in scientific research. ... it is important to acknowledge the role of human oversight in guiding and interpreting the results, ensuring that the final output maintains the depth required in scholarly research.

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: Limitation: The initial search strategy was suboptimal due to absence of comprehensive Boolean operators (lack of 'AND' in search strings), potentially compromising specificity and thoroughness of the literature search.
evidence_quote: the initial search strategy employed for identifying relevant literature was sub optimal. The absence of a comprehensive use of Boolean operators, notably the lack of 'AND' in the search strings, potentially compromised the specificity and thoroughness of the literature search

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: Limitation: No clearly defined criteria for primary and secondary exclusion, and the data extraction reliability is questionable due to lack of a robust analytical algorithm.
evidence_quote: a significant gap in its approach to literature selection, characterized by an absence of clearly defined criteria for primary and secondary exclusion ... the reliability of the extracted information is questionable due to the lack of a robust analytical algorithm.

title: System for Systematic Literature Review Using Multi-AI Agent System
claim_text: Future work will address search strategy refinement, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, advanced data extraction algorithms (ML/NLP), robust analytical frameworks, broader literature scope, and stakeholder engagement.
evidence_quote: Refinement of search strategy ... Implementation of explicit exclusion and inclusion criteria ... Advancement of data extraction methods ... Enhancement of analytical framework ... Broadening of literature scope ... Stakeholder engagement

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: All prompts and LLM outputs are publicly available on Zenodo for reproducibility purposes.
evidence_quote: All prompts and LLM outputs used in this study are publicly available on Zenodo for reproducibility purposes at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14177022.

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Verification was applied through cross-checking among human reviewers (manual) and double-checking via comparison with manual results plus review of discrepancies (LLM-assisted).
evidence_quote: Verification Applied: Cross-checking among human reviewers (Manual) / Double-checking: comparison with manual results + review of discrepancies (LLM-Assisted Execution)
section: Table 1 (Comparison of Manual vs. LLM-Assisted Execution)

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: LLM achieved approximately 95% accuracy in screening (208/219 correct) but 11 hallucination cases were identified where the model answered with information from other works; extraction accuracy was 92.3% (12/13 correct) with 1 error.
evidence_quote: the LLM achieved approximately 95.0% accuracy (208 correct out of 219 studies), with 11 hallucination cases in which it began answering the questionnaire with information from other works. In the data extraction stage, the LLM reached approximately 92% accuracy (12 correct out of 13 studies), with 1 error identified.

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Prompt design sensitivity was demonstrated: the screening prompt was refined 4 times and extraction prompt refined 6 times to improve precision and reduce ambiguity, showing LLM performance is highly sensitive to prompt wording.
evidence_quote: the screening prompt was refined four times and the extraction prompt six times to improve precision and reduce ambiguity, demonstrating the sensitivity of LLM performance to prompt wording.

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Hybrid workflows are essential: LLMs should be embedded in workflows combining partial automation with targeted human supervision — complete delegation risks loss of methodological rigor.
evidence_quote: LLMs should be integrated cautiously and deliberately, as complementary tools within human-centered workflows. Their value lies in supporting efficiency in operational stages, while preserving direct engagement with the source material as a prerequisite for trustworthy interpretation and synthesis.

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Time reduction was substantial: manual screening took ~23 days, LLM-assisted screening took ~9 hours (98% reduction); manual extraction took ~7 days, LLM-assisted took ~1 hour (99% reduction).
evidence_quote: the complete manual process of screening and data extraction required approximately 23 days for the screening of 219 studies and 7 days for the data extraction of 13 studies ... the process supported by the LLM was completed in approximately 9 hours for screening the 219 studies and 1 hour for extracting data from 13 studies, representing a significant reduction

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: LLM effectiveness is task-dependent: Gemini PRO achieved 90% in extraction and screening, Manus 98% in screening but only 40% in extraction, and Copilot 60% in both — model selection should be treated as a methodological decision.
evidence_quote: Manus correctly classified 49 (98%), Gemini PRO 45 (90%), and Copilot 30 (60%). In the data extraction process ... Manus achieved 4 correct (40%), Gemini PRO 9 (90%), and Copilot 6 (60%). ... LLM effectiveness is task-dependent and cannot be assumed to be consistent across different stages.

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Limitation: The study reflects the experience of a single researcher; sample size for data extraction was small (13 studies); manual and LLM-assisted executions were conducted in different periods, limiting generalizability.
evidence_quote: This experience report is subject to limitations related to sample size and scope ... the data extraction phase was conducted on a smaller subset of 13 studies ... the procedures, challenges, and outcomes reflect the experience of a single researcher ... manual and LLM-assisted executions were performed in different time periods.
section: Section 5.2 (Sample Size and Scope Limitations) / Section 7

title: On the Use of a Large Language Model to Support a Systematic Mapping Study: A Practitioner's View
claim_text: Five lessons learned: (1) time efficiency is significant but contextual, (2) prompt design is critical, (3) human oversight remains essential, (4) hybrid workflows are the way forward, (5) Gemini PRO shows promise.
evidence_quote: Lesson 1: Time Efficiency is Significant but Contextual ... Lesson 2: Prompt Design is Critical ... Lesson 3: Human Oversight Remains Essential ... Lesson 4: Hybrid Workflows are the Way Forward ... Lesson 5: Gemini PRO Shows Promise

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: The proposed RAG architecture integrates Azure Blob Storage (crawling/storage), Azure AI Search (embedding/indexing), and Azure OpenAI (LLM generation) with custom Python automation tools, forming an end-to-end pipeline from data acquisition to aggregated responses.
evidence_quote: The solution architecture used in this study aggregates: crawling, cloud storage, embedding, indexing, LLM, and automation services ... integrating mature software tools as Azure AI Search (for embeddings and vector spaces) and OpenAI for language processing, with complementary custom Python tools developed for automating and scaling up the entire process

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: A progressive five-step testing methodology was implemented, scaling from 1 article with 10 manual questions (Experiment #1) to 30 articles with 10 AI-generated cross-document synthesis questions (Experiment #5).
evidence_quote: The implementation strategy has 5 incremental steps, meant to evaluate the solution progressively, from small functional tests to a large-scale volume testing.

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Feeding curated data via Azure AI Search to the LLM is described as the first step for avoiding hallucinations; the LLM is instructed to return citations linked to response, pointing to original documents — a decisive factor for raising trust.
evidence_quote: feeding curated data via Azure AI Search to an LLM is the first step. The LLM model will receive a specific context, a specific prompt and it will respond only with information from the private data to queries. In will also be instructed to return citations linked to the response, pointing to the places in the original documents where the info was taken, a decisive factor for raising the trust on the solution.

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Temperature was decreased to 0.1 (from default 0.7) and Top P set to 0.95 to maximize precision and restrict the model to high-probability tokens, with the Assistant instructed to answer only from custom indexed information.
evidence_quote: The standard Temperature value of 0.7, was decreased to 0.1, since the intention of the solution is to deliver very precise answers, based only on the information indexed into Azure AI. In the same direction, Top P value used was 0.95, so only high probability tokens will be considered when building the response.

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Validation results ranged from 76% (Romanian, Exp #1) to 94% (AI-generated English, Exp #4), with Romanian consistently performing worse than English (~90-95% gap); cross-document synthesis questions yielded slightly lower results.
evidence_quote: Experiment # 1 Manually generated 76% 80% Researcher # 2 Manually generated 80% 100% Researcher # 3 Manually generated - 85% Researcher # 4 AI generated - 94% Gemini 1.5 Pro # 5 AI generated - 81% Gemini 1.5 Pro ... Romanian questions were more troublesome than the English ones, independently of the models used

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Manual synthesis of 30 articles is estimated at 50+ hours; the same task was completed in 1 minute 24 seconds using the RAG architecture, demonstrating orders-of-magnitude time reduction.
evidence_quote: Multiplying this value with 30 articles (our experiment #5 dataset size), the overall estimated effort for manually analysis can reach more than 50 hours, while the time needed to obtain the responses on the experiment #5 was 1 minute and 24 seconds.

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Limitation: All cloud services carry associated costs (Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI, Blob Storage, Compute) that must be assessed before implementation; data privacy concerns require that research data remain logically isolated and not used for model training by the cloud provider.
evidence_quote: all cloud services come with an associated cost ... Other important point of attention for adopting a solution like the one proposed in this article, is mainly related to ethics, and the assurance that data remains private ... the data should not be used to train any other models, main or private, by the cloud owner

title: Advanced Semantic Analysis of Research Papers Using a Retrieval-Augmented Architecture
claim_text: Future work should prioritize designing sophisticated testing frameworks to reconfirm reliability; Agentic AI is anticipated as an evolution that will independently orchestrate crawling and RAG analysis but will face navigation drifts, hallucinations, increased costs, and security concerns.
evidence_quote: future works should prioritize the design of sophisticated testing ways to reconfirm the reliability of the proposed solution. An evolution that can be easily anticipated today ... is the usage of Agentic AIs ... that will be able to perform end-to-end crawling and RAG analysis. ... Agentic AIs will most probably face several challenges such as navigation drifts or hallucinations, increased costs, or security concerns.
